patterns.title: Destination state navigation
patterns.intent: Keep navigation location and selection understandable across expanded, collapsed, and compact navigation surfaces.
patterns.problem_or_context: Navigation controls may change shape or density while still needing an explicit current destination.
patterns.recommended_behavior: Preserve a single clear active destination state and keep primary and secondary destinations distinguishable when navigation compresses or expands.
accessibility_constraints: Use native links or buttons when the destination or trigger is interactive.
Do not rely on icon position, animation, or styling alone to identify the active destination.

patterns.title: Contextual navigation and shortcuts
patterns.intent: Expose useful secondary navigation and temporal shortcuts without obscuring the primary navigation model.
patterns.problem_or_context: Users often need secondary destinations or shortcuts such as today/current-context actions in addition to primary movement controls.
patterns.recommended_behavior: Keep contextual shortcuts visually and semantically subordinate to the primary navigation control while making the resulting selected context explicit.
accessibility_constraints: Use controls with programmatic names for shortcuts and navigation triggers.
Selected context must be perceivable without requiring color alone.

patterns.title: Authentication and multi-step form flow
patterns.intent: Keep mode changes and multi-step progress explicit while grouping related inputs and local validation.
patterns.problem_or_context: Authentication modes and long forms can hide where the user is, what belongs together, and what must be corrected before continuing.
patterns.recommended_behavior: Group fields by task, show the current mode or step, validate at the smallest useful scope, and preserve clear Back, Next, Submit, login, and signup transitions.
accessibility_constraints: Use native form controls and associated labels.
Step and mode state must be announced or otherwise programmatically determinable.

patterns.title: Semantic field and control state
patterns.intent: Make field, toggle, radio, and submission states explicit without sacrificing native semantics.
patterns.problem_or_context: Custom visual controls can communicate state well visually while losing labels, keyboard behavior, or programmatic state.
patterns.recommended_behavior: Preserve native input, radio, checkbox, and button semantics first; layer visual state feedback on top of associated labels and explicit control state.
accessibility_constraints: Do not replace labels with placeholder-only text.
Do not replace native radio, checkbox, or button semantics with generic click targets.
State-changing controls require an accessible name that remains meaningful in every state.

patterns.title: Selection and disclosure state
patterns.intent: Keep one-of-many selection and expandable disclosure state explicit and reversible.
patterns.problem_or_context: Calendars, radio groups, settings accordions, and similar controls need clear selected, expanded, and collapsed state without ambiguous generic click behavior.
patterns.recommended_behavior: Use the semantic control appropriate to the interaction, keep selected and expanded state explicit, and preserve a predictable path back to the unselected or collapsed state.
accessibility_constraints: Use buttons for disclosure triggers and native radio semantics for single-choice groups.
Expose selected or expanded state programmatically where the control model supports it.

patterns.title: Operation progress lifecycle
patterns.intent: Represent long-running or multi-stage operations as explicit state transitions with measurable progress when available.
patterns.problem_or_context: Uploads, aggregate payments, progress controls, and multi-step forms can leave users uncertain whether work has started, paused, advanced, or completed.
patterns.recommended_behavior: Expose a stable operation identity, current state, and numeric or step progress when meaningful; distinguish running, paused, completed, and aggregate progress rather than treating progress as decoration.
accessibility_constraints: Progress must have a textual or programmatic equivalent when visualized.
Pause, resume, and completion state must not be conveyed by animation alone.

patterns.title: Outcome feedback and empty state
patterns.intent: Tell users when a task has no data, fails validation, succeeds, or completes.
patterns.problem_or_context: Interfaces that only show the active task can leave users without a clear terminal or no-content state.
patterns.recommended_behavior: Model empty, validation-error, success, and completion outcomes as explicit states with concise next-step information where action is possible.
accessibility_constraints: Outcome messages must be available to assistive technology when they change dynamically.
Do not rely on color or transient motion as the only success or error signal.

patterns.title: Action priority and destructive separation
patterns.intent: Make primary, secondary, routine, overflow, and destructive actions distinguishable before activation.
patterns.problem_or_context: Dense action groups can obscure the main task or place destructive actions too close to routine actions.
patterns.recommended_behavior: Promote one primary task when appropriate, group secondary or social actions separately, and visually and semantically separate destructive actions from routine operations.
accessibility_constraints: Action triggers require explicit accessible names.
Destructive meaning must not depend on color alone and should receive confirmation or recovery treatment appropriate to risk.

patterns.title: Dense summary and status hierarchy
patterns.intent: Lead with the current summary while keeping supporting metrics, per-entity status, and detail scan-friendly.
patterns.problem_or_context: Financial, weather, and commerce surfaces combine a primary summary with multiple supporting facts and status signals.
patterns.recommended_behavior: Establish a primary summary, group supporting metrics by meaning, and keep per-entity or fulfillment status scannable without flattening all values to equal visual weight.
accessibility_constraints: Preserve meaningful reading order independent of visual placement.
Images that carry information require useful alternative text.

patterns.title: Content summary card and call to action
patterns.intent: Group related identity, offer, product, or profile information around one understandable action hierarchy.
patterns.problem_or_context: Cards often combine identity or offer metadata, secondary attributes, and one or more actions in limited space.
patterns.recommended_behavior: Group title or identity, essential metadata, supporting attributes, and action area in a stable reading order; avoid making decorative treatment the organizing principle.
accessibility_constraints: Images require appropriate alternative text when informative.
Icon-only social or secondary actions must be real links or buttons with accessible names.

patterns.title: Ordered collection and temporal sequence
patterns.intent: Keep repeated items understandable as an ordered collection with clear item state and sequence context.
patterns.problem_or_context: Notifications, forecasts, and task lists present repeated content where order, completion, or time affects meaning.
patterns.recommended_behavior: Use a consistent item anatomy, expose temporal or completion metadata when relevant, and provide a meaningful empty state for collections that may contain no items.
accessibility_constraints: Preserve logical DOM order for ordered content.
Scroll or motion effects must not be required to understand item order or state.

patterns.title: Semantic control accessibility baseline
patterns.intent: Preserve useful interaction models while rejecting accessibility regressions observed in reference implementations.
patterns.problem_or_context: Several references use generic div or list elements, missing labels, or unlabeled icon controls for interactions that have native semantic equivalents.
patterns.recommended_behavior: Choose native links, buttons, inputs, labels, radio controls, checkboxes, and disclosure semantics first; add custom styling only after keyboard, naming, state, and focus behavior are preserved.
accessibility_constraints: Generic click targets must not replace native interactive semantics when a native control fits.
Every informative icon or interactive icon control requires context-appropriate accessible naming.
Form fields require associated labels rather than placeholder-only naming.

patterns.title: Motion as secondary state feedback
patterns.intent: Use motion to reinforce state change without making animation the only carrier of meaning.
patterns.problem_or_context: Animated navigation, notification stacks, progress controls, visibility toggles, and field treatments can make state change noticeable but can also obscure semantics or create motion sensitivity issues.
patterns.recommended_behavior: Pair motion with persistent text, state, position, or control semantics; provide reduced-motion treatment when motion is substantial and never use motion as the sole active, progress, or completion indicator.
accessibility_constraints: Respect reduced-motion preferences for substantial non-essential animation.
State must remain understandable with animation disabled.

patterns.title: Explicit state labels and metadata
patterns.intent: Pair visual state with concise labels or metadata that explain what changed and what the user is seeing.
patterns.problem_or_context: Files, payment summaries, notifications, visibility controls, weather forecasts, and validation flows use small metadata elements to disambiguate state.
patterns.recommended_behavior: Expose concise identity, status, time, progress, or state labels next to the element they explain, and update those labels consistently with the underlying state model.
accessibility_constraints: Metadata that changes task meaning must be available to assistive technology.
Do not encode state solely through icon shape or color.

patterns.title: General UI icon system
patterns.intent: Use a coherent general-purpose icon vocabulary with consistent geometry and explicit semantic treatment.
patterns.problem_or_context: General UI icon libraries offer broad reusable vocabularies but require consistent selection, accessible semantics, and applicable license notices.
patterns.recommended_behavior: Prefer a consistent icon family and visual grammar within a product surface, distinguish informative from decorative icons, and preserve applicable MIT or ISC notice obligations for direct reuse.
accessibility_constraints: Informative icons need context-appropriate accessible names or adjacent text.
Decorative icons should be hidden from assistive technology when they add no semantic information.

patterns.title: Brand icon traceability and rights
patterns.intent: Keep brand icon source identity and brand-rights review separate from general UI icon reuse.
patterns.problem_or_context: Copyright permission for a brand-icon asset does not automatically clear trademark, endorsement, sponsorship, or brand-guideline concerns.
patterns.recommended_behavior: Retain source metadata and guideline links for brand icons, require context-specific rights review before use, and avoid treating CC0 copyright status as a blanket trademark permission.
accessibility_constraints: Use context-appropriate accessible names when a brand icon communicates identity or action.
Hide purely decorative brand marks from assistive technology only when the surrounding content already provides equivalent identity.
